key_insight: Using Mask R-CNN for instance-level segmentation yields pixel-accurate masks of thin, branching pavement cracks, enabling geometry-preserving measurements (length, area, connectivity) that image-level labels or bounding boxes cannot provide.
problem_solved: Automated pavement distress assessment requires precise localization of irregular, thin, and branching cracks for maintenance-relevant quantification; prior image-level or bounding-box approaches lack the geometric precision needed for accurate measurements.
method: Adapt Mask R-CNN to detect and produce instance masks for pavement distress on field-collected roadway images (UWGB-StreetCrack dataset).
Train and evaluate using pixel-level metrics (e.g., mask IoU / F-measure) and demonstrate improved geometric localization vs. box/label baselines.
Post-process masks to extract maintenance metrics (crack length, width, area, and connectivity) suitable for infrastructure decision-making.
impact: Delivers a practical computer-vision pipeline that converts raw road imagery into measurement-quality crack geometry, enabling more accurate, automated maintenance prioritization and scalable pavement monitoring for practitioners.
visual_elements: Before/after image: raw road photo beside Mask R-CNN overlay with colored instance masks highlighting thin branching cracks.
Pipeline diagram: capture → annotation → Mask R-CNN → mask post-processing → maintenance metrics (length/area/connectivity).
Bar/line chart: comparison of pixel-level accuracy (IoU/F1) and geometric errors versus classification/bounding-box baselines.
Icon set: vehicle-mounted camera, annotation tool, segmentation mask, and maintenance decision icon to convey end-to-end value.
paper_title: Pixel-Level Pavement Distress Assessment Using Instance Segmentation
paper_authors: Logan Dewick, Bibesh Pyakurel, Kong Pheng Yang, Nazim Choudhury, M. G. Sarwar Murshed
